Satellite radiance observation error inflation and spatial thinning: Reconciling idealized theory with near‐operational applications
nodes.venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
nodes.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the joint effects of spatial thinning and observation error standard deviation inflation in satellite radiance assimilation, focusing on the common operational setting in which true observation errors are spatially correlated but are assumed to be uncorrelated. Idealized diagnostics are combined with near‐operational experiments from a global deterministic prediction system to reconcile theory and operational practice, providing a unified, physically based interpretation of thinning–inflation interactions and highlighting the underlying mechanisms governing their relationship. An idealized data assimilation framework, scaled to operationally relevant spatial characteristics, is used to diagnose how optimal inflation depends on thinning distance and on background and observation error correlation length scales. Results reveal a robust asymptotic behavior: when both background and observation error correlation length scales exceed the thinning distance, the optimal inflation approaches the square root of the ratio of the thinning distance. Spectral diagnostics explains this behavior and clarifies why the inflation saturates, providing a physical basis for commonly observed empirical tuning values. Conversely, when the observation error correlation length scale is short relative to the thinning distance, the optimal inflation remains close to unity. These theoretical results are evaluated in a near‐operational context using 15 experimental configurations over a 2.5‐month period, with thinning distances of 150 and 100 km and a range of inflation factors. Reducing thinning without inflation improves the analysis fit to radiances while degrading the fits to several other assimilated observation types and forecast performance, suggesting an excessive influence of the radiances. Increasing the inflation by factors of about 1.4–1.5 mitigates this behavior. Forecast scores demonstrate statistically significant improvements when thinning reduction is paired with appropriate inflation, particularly in the tropics and Southern Hemisphere. Overall, near‐operational results are broadly consistent with the mechanisms identified in the idealized framework, suggesting that these remain relevant in more realistic assimilation systems despite their greater complexity.

nodes.name: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
Robust Satellite Techniques for Detecting and Monitoring Icebergs by Sentinel-2 Data
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: In recent decades, the sharp rise in global temperatures has accelerated the melting of the polar ice caps, causing icebergs to break off and subsequently drift across the sea surface. At the same time, the increase in navigable areas in the Arctic region has led to a continued growth in maritime traffic at higher latitudes, resulting in a consequent increase in the risk of iceberg–ship collisions. In this context, it is particularly important to provide vessels at sea with timely and up-to-date information on the presence of icebergs along routes in mid- and high-latitude waters. Given this challenge, this paper presents, for the first time, the Robust Satellite Techniques (RST) methodology employed at the global level to perform iceberg detection using imagery acquired only in the B3 band (centred at 560 nm) by the Sentinel-2 (S2) constellation. A test performed near Greenland (in September 2016) and in the Labrador Sea (in August 2021), showed that, in comparison with traditional fixed-threshold methods, this approach (easily implementable in the Google Earth Engine cloud platform) demonstrated: (a) very high sensitivity by doubling the number of detected icebergs (including the smaller ones); (b) high reliability with an overall false positive below 20% that becomes zero when other objects that may pose a hazard to navigation (e.g., dark ships, shallow reefs, etc.) are also considered.

nodes.name: Recurrent neural network-based collaborative perception method for robot multimodal sensors
nodes.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Learning (ICRL 2026)
nodes.abstract: With the advancement of industrial automation and intelligent manufacturing, robots are increasingly requiredtoperform collaborative perception of their own operating status and external working environment in scenarios suchasassembly, inspection, operation & maintenance and human-robot collaboration. However, multi-modal sensors onrobotsexhibit significant heterogeneity in sampling rate, physical dimension, noise characteristics and information density, which makes it difficult for conventional time-series models to simultaneously cope with long-term dependencies, cross-modal coupling and physical consistency. This paper proposes a recurrent neural network based collaborative perceptionmethod for robot multi-modal sensors. The method builds an internal multi-physics branch and an external context branch to perform intra-modal temporal modeling and semantic infomation extraction respectively; a three-headattention mechanism (self, external and additive) is introduced to achieve dynamic cross-modal fusion; a DiffusionConvolutional Recurrent Neural Network (DCRNN) is further coupled to realize joint spatio-temporal modeling over thesensor node graph; self-supervised pre-training and multi-task learning are adopted, with the residual of partial differential equations introduced as a physical consistency loss. Experiments on five industrial datasets across fourprediction horizons show that the proposed method consistently outperforms Prophet, single-branch LSTMand DCRNNbaselines on MAE, RMSE, MAPE and R² metrics, and the advantage becomes more significant as the prediction horizongrows, verifying the effectiveness of the "recurrent backbone + attention fusion + physical constraint" frameworkforrobot multi-modal collaborative perception.

nodes.name: International Conference on Robotics and Learning (ICRL 2026)
Physics-Guided and Horizon-Aware Dynamic Liquid-Level Identification and Forecasting in Oil Wells Using Distributed Temperature Sensing
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Accurate dynamic liquid-level monitoring in rod-pumped oil wells requires not only reliable identification of the gas–liquid interface from distributed sensing data but also stable forecasting over extended horizons. This study develops a physics-guided and horizon-aware PatchTST framework (PGH-PatchTST) for dynamic liquid-level identification and forecasting based on distributed temperature sensing (DTS). The measured time–depth–temperature field is reconstructed and denoised, and the gas–liquid interface is localized using the maximum absolute spatial temperature gradient. Unlike the previous multiscale formulation that uses only the derived liquid-level sequence and fixed multiscale feature fusion, PGH-PatchTST incorporates liquid-level depth, temperature-gradient magnitude, peak-dominance index, and liquid-level variation rate as DTS-aware state features. A physics-guided routing mechanism adaptively weights patch representations at lengths of 8, 16, and 24 samples. In addition, a horizon-aware trend–residual forecasting branch adjusts the contributions of local fluctuations and long-term trends according to the forecasting distance, aiming to reduce systematic degradation at long horizons. The proposed framework demonstrated improved forecasting performance compared with representative time-series forecasting models, while the horizon-aware mechanism effectively alleviated systematic deviation during long-horizon prediction.

nodes.name: Multimodal radiomics based on dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound for predicting cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Oncology
nodes.abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal predictive model by integrating radiomic features from B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (DCE-US) parametric imaging, as well as clinical and conventional ultrasound features, for preoperative prediction of cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT) complicated with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Methods A total of 191 patients with pathologically confirmed HT-complicated PTC were retrospectively enrolled between December 2023 and July 2025. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n=133) and a validation set (n=58) at a 7:3 ratio using a random number generator. Radiomic features were extracted from BMUS images and DCE-US peak enhancement parametric maps. Feature stability was assessed using intraclass and interclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Key features were selected through a sequential process including the Mann–Whitney U test, recursive feature elimination (RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by calculation of the radiomics score (Rad-score). Independent predictors of CLNM were identified using multivariate logistic regression incorporating clinical and ultrasound features. Three predictive models were constructed: a clinical-ultrasound model, a radiomics model, and a combined multi-modal model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis. Results TG-Ab, TR-Ab, extrathyroidal extension, filling defects, BMUS Rad-score, and DCE-US Rad-score were independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the training and validation sets, the combined model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.936 and 0.916, respectively, which were significantly higher than those of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.825, 0.876) and the clinical-ultrasound model (AUC = 0.760, 0.800; DeLong test, P < 0.05). Calibration curves showed good model fitting. DCA confirmed that the combined model provided greater clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI verified that the combined model significantly improved CLNM prediction performance. SHAP analysis revealed that DCE-US Rad-score was the most important predictor for CLNM. Conclusion A multi-modal predictive model combining dual-modality ultrasound radiomic scores (BMUS and DCE-US) with clinical and ultrasound features can effectively and robustly predict CLNM in patients with HT-complicated PTC and performs better than single-modal models. This model provides an objective reference for the formulation of individualized surgical strategies.

nodes.name: Morphology-guided dual-level detection and depth localization of cotton terminal buds for precision topping
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: Reliable terminal-bud localization is essential for precision cotton topping, yet the small bud core is often obscured by apical leaves and visually confounded with the surrounding canopy. We developed DGQ-YOLO, a lightweight morphology-guided detector that jointly identifies the bud core and a composite terminal-bud region encompassing the core and adjacent apical leaves. This dual-level representation preserves structural cues when the bud core is partly occluded. The model combines C2f_DWR_CA for multiscale, position-sensitive feature extraction, VoVGS-CA for lightweight feature fusion, and QCN loss for quality-aware classification and small-object regression. DGQ-YOLO was evaluated using 2,230 field images of long-staple cotton at the early bud-development stage. It achieved mAP@50 values of 93.2% and 94.1% for the bud core and composite terminal-bud region, respectively. Overall mAP@50 and mAP@50:95 were 93.6% and 81.7%, respectively. Compared with YOLOv8n, DGQ-YOLO improved overall mAP@50 by 2.2 percentage points. Its parameter count decreased from 3.01 to 2.90 million, and its computational cost fell from 8.2 to 7.8 GFLOPs. Combining the centers of the two detected regions with RGB-D depth measurements supported online terminal-bud localization in field experiments. This morphology-informed perception framework supports precision topping under the tested cultivar, developmental stage, and field conditions, although broader agronomic and actuator-level validation is required.

nodes.name: Mapping Soil Salinity in Arid Agricultural Regions Using Multi-Source Remote Sensing and a Long-Range Dependency-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework
nodes.venue: Land
nodes.abstract: Soil salinity estimation across arid agricultural regions is challenging due to pronounced environmental heterogeneity and complex dependencies among multi-source variables. This study proposes a Long-Range Dependency-Enhanced Network (LRD-Net) for regional-scale soil salinity estimation in multiple agricultural oasis regions using multi-source remote sensing and environmental covariates. A dataset comprising 180 field samples from three agricultural oasis regions in Xinjiang, China, was constructed with 25 covariates derived from spectral, topographic, climatic, and soil property data. LRD-Net consists of three stages: a multi-scale feature fusion backbone based on depthwise separable convolutions and cross-scale interaction; a Long-Range Dependency Enhancement Module (LDEM) with an asymmetric dual-branch architecture that captures forward and reverse-aware dependencies through reverse alignment and cross-directional fusion; and multi-scale attention refinement with a regression head for continuous salinity estimation. Under the region-stratified random-split evaluation, LRD-Net achieved an R2 of 0.905, an RMSE of 1.207 g·kg−1, and an MAE of 0.868 g·kg−1. Performance decreased under more spatially independent validation, with an R2 of 0.874 under spatial cross-validation and LORO test R2 values ranging from 0.739 to 0.801, indicating that prediction across spatially and geographically independent samples is more challenging than region-stratified random-split evaluation. The proposed framework effectively integrates multi-source information and captures complementary long-range dependencies, providing a potential approach for regional-scale soil salinity estimation within the studied arid agricultural oasis environments and supporting soil salinization monitoring and sustainable land management in the study region.

nodes.name: MSTDP: Multimodal Spatio-Temporal Forecasting with Self-Correcting Attention and Hierarchical Feature Interaction
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Real-world spatiotemporal data are frequently imbalanced across spatial regions and collected from heterogeneous sources with different structures, sampling frequencies, and semantics. Sparse regions provide limited supervision, whereas modality redundancy and structural heterogeneity make it difficult to exploit complementary information during fusion. To address these challenges, we propose MSTDP, a Multimodal Spatio-Temporal Data Prediction framework. A causal target-clock alignment procedure first maps high-frequency, low-frequency, and irregular observations to the forecasting timeline without using future information. MSTDP then employs modality-specific encoders to obtain source-dependent representations and constructs first-, second-, and third-order interaction features through a Multilayer Feature Interaction module. A Hierarchical Feature Fusion module aggregates the interaction features. To improve intermediate and high-level representations, we further introduce two plug-and-play components: a Unified Feature Interaction Module, which performs soft alignment and bidirectional feature exchange between heterogeneous token sequences, and a Self-Correcting Transformer Module, which recalibrates modality-specific and fused representations through cross-modal attention. A spatial-unit-balanced training objective first normalizes the prediction error within each region and then averages equally across regions, preventing data-rich regions from dominating the gradients. We evaluate MSTDP on four real-world benchmarks covering urban housing-price forecasting, county-level crop-yield prediction, and traffic-speed forecasting. Relative to the strongest baseline in each setting, MSTDP reduces RMSE by up to 8.6% and MAPE by up to 11.5%. Ablation studies confirm that hierarchical fusion, unified feature interaction, and self-correction provide complementary improvements. Observation-density stress tests further show that the model remains robust when entire spatial units are unavailable. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MSTDP on the four evaluated datasets and provide empirical evidence that its interaction and correction modules can be reused across the studied housing, agriculture, and traffic forecasting tasks. Broader transferability to other multisource spatiotemporal problems remains to be established.

nodes.name: LGTM: A Time Series Model for Large-Scale Geospatial Land Subsidence Prediction
nodes.abstract: Land subsidence threatens infrastructure, ecosystems and coastal communities, yet predicting its spatially heterogeneous evolution from long-term interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) imagery remains challenging. Here, we propose the Large-scale Geospatial Time-series Model (LGTM), a spatiotemporal fusion network that combines a dual-path Informer-p temporal encoder with a simplified U-Net spatial decoder to model long-range temporal dependencies and multiscale spatial patterns. Using 136 cumulative SBAS-InSAR deformation images acquired from 10 January 2018 to 1 June 2023 in the Yellow River Delta, China, we evaluated three approximately 943.7 km² subregions representing circular subsidence funnels, irregular patches and radially contiguous subsidence clusters. Under identical data partitions, normalization procedures, training protocols and evaluation masks, LGTM was compared with ConvLSTM, TimesNet and BiLSTM, while ablation experiments examined Informer, Informer-p and Informer+U-Net. LGTM achieved the highest structural similarity index (SSIM) in all three regions, whereas histogram intersection over union (IoU) and normalized cross-correlation (NCC) were highest or tied for highest. The largest relative reduction in root mean square error (RMSE) and increases in SSIM, IoU and NCC were 36.90%, 7.57%, 3.10% and 6.39%, respectively. Although LGTM did not achieve the lowest RMSE in every region, it consistently outperformed Informer+U-Net across all four metrics in the ablation experiments. Informer-p alone did not consistently outperform the original Informer, indicating that the observed gains were associated primarily with the joint temporal-spatial fusion. These results demonstrate that LGTM provides a balanced approach to numerical prediction and preservation of complex subsidence structures in regional InSAR time-series forecasting.

nodes.name: KAN-Mamba U-Net: synergistic integration of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and Mamba for efficient medical image segmentation
nodes.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Learning (ICRL 2026)
nodes.abstract: Medical image segmentation is a cornerstone of CAD. High precision and computational efficiency still present certain challenges. Conventional architectures such as CNNs and Transformers have difficulty in jointly modeling complex local non-linearities, long-range spatial dependencies and diverse anatomical structures. We introduce KAN-Mamba U-Net, a hybrid encoder-decoder architecture that integrates KANs and Mamba SSMs. The core module KAN-Mamba Block has parallel KAN and Mamba branches to capture complex non-linear feature relationships and global context. Attention-enhanced skip connections optimize cross-level feature fusion. Experiments are conducted on four public benchmarks (BUSI, Kvasir-Seg, GlaS, and Synapse). Our model achieves state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy on the Synapse multi-organ task, with a mean Dice score of 89.5%, while requiring only 18.6 GFLOPs and 8.7Mparameters.

nodes.name: HexaClus: Uncertainty-Aware Hexagonal Supervised Spatial Clustering++
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Due to the heterogeneity and uneven distribution of geospatial data, predictive geospatial techniques are often required to provide both accurate target predictions and uncertainty quantification. However, existing approaches typically only provide post-hoc uncertainty estimates, rather than using uncertainty to guide the spatial model training process itself. To address these limitations, we introduce HexaClus++, a supervised, uncertainty-aware, spatial-clustering-based approach that integrates both accuracy and uncertainty to guide local model training on clustered spatial hexagonal regions. To evaluate the performance of our technique, we conduct experiments on property valuation datasets using diverse machine learning approaches. The results demonstrate that HexaClus++, when combined with different base learners, achieves competitive accuracy while also delivering well-calibrated uncertainty, reliable prediction intervals, and enhanced interpretability through regional uncertainty maps and spatially varying feature importance.

nodes.name: HFA-Net: hierarchical fusion attention network for remote sensing image change detection
nodes.venue: Journal of Applied Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing image change detection plays a crucial role in fields such as urban planning and land use. However, existing methods often face challenges such as class imbalance, pseudo-change interference, and the difficulty of balancing computational efficiency with detection accuracy. To address these issues, this article proposes a hierarchical fusion attention network (HFA-Net). This network adopts a symmetric encoder–decoder architecture and integrates four key modules to enhance performance. First, we design the grouped multi-scale attention module to efficiently capture multi-scale context information within a single computational path and adaptively enhance key features. Second, we construct a multilevel feature fusion mechanism, including the efficient residual feature interaction module for early feature enhancement, the adjacent-scale feature aggregation module to fuse deep semantic and shallow details within a single temporal image, and the shared channel–spatial feature attention module to dynamically fuse bitemporal features using shared weights during the decoding stage. These modules work together to precisely suppress pseudo-changes, enhance real change features, and effectively balance computational efficiency and representation capability of the model. Experimental results on three public datasets show that HFA-Net achieves F1-scores of 92.13%, 83.41%, and 86.21% on the LEVIR-CD, SYSU-CD, and GZ-CD datasets, respectively. Compared with the best-performing competing method on each dataset, HFA-Net improves the F1-score by 0.89, 0.44, and 0.06 percentage points and the Intersection over Union by 1.52, 0.62, and 0.07 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of HFA-Net for accurate and robust change detection in complex scenes.

nodes.name: Gas Lift Evaluation and Production Forecasting Through a Transfer Learning Dual-Track Machine Learning Framework
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract As reservoirs deplete and natural flow declines, artificial lift becomes necessary to sustain production, and gas lift is one of the most applied methods in unconventional horizontal wells. Injecting high-pressure gas lowers the density of the flowing column and increases drawdown, but the production response is not proportional to the gas injected. It is governed by nonlinear interactions among injection rate, wellbore pressures, geometry, and fluid properties. Beyond an optimum, additional gas reduces production. Machine learning captures such relationships well and predicts oil rate with high accuracy, yet that accuracy is almost always measured within the same wells a model was trained on. A companion study of 11 Eagle Ford wells (Al Raisi et al., 2026) reported R2 as high as 0.960 under a random split but strongly negative values under leave-one-well-out (LOWO) evaluation, because field measurements cluster in a narrow band of conditions and much of the gas lift domain is never observed. This study's framework combines two tracks. Track A applies data-driven models to daily field data from the 11 wells. Track B uses a steady-state multiphase flow simulator to build a physics-consistent synthetic dataset in two complementary designs: a broad dataset of 6,000 nodal-analysis cases sampled by Latin Hypercube Sampling, establishing which operating conditions exist and where gas lift helps, and a controlled sweep of 700 scenarios evaluated at 11 injection rates each, resolving how production responds to injection. Together these required 13,700 simulation cases. A deep learning neural network is then trained through a staged transfer learning procedure that pre-trains on the broad dataset, refines on the sweep dataset, and fine-tunes on field data. The simulations reproduce established gas lift behavior, which is what makes them usable as a training signal. Feasibility rises from 90% to 99% with gas lift, 285 of 295 otherwise non-productive cases are enabled, and the resulting performance curves fall into monotonic, plateau, and post-peak decline classes separated by tubing size, wellhead pressure, and fluid properties. Under LOWO evaluation, staged transfer learning raises the average R2 from 0.149 to 0.414, reduces MAE from 70 to 56 STB/D, and lowers MAPE from 56% to 38%. Neither dataset suffices alone: broad-only pre-training yields 0.146 and sweep-only 0.322, so breadth and structure are both required and the order matters. The gains concentrate on wells the baseline fails, most notably Well 4, which moves from a strongly negative to a positive R2. Applied to a well-level injection scenario, the model ranks lift responsiveness across operating states in the physically expected order, supporting open-loop screening and gas allocation. The study also reports a useful negative result: despite 135 post-peak-decline scenarios in training, predicted curves rise monotonically and do not reproduce over-injection. Expanded coverage and explicit physical constraints are therefore complementary rather than interchangeable.

nodes.name: From Reactive to Proactive: A Physics-Guided Cross-Well Knowledge Coupling Framework for Stuck-Pipe Early Warning
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Stuck pipe is a major risk in complex deep drilling. Conventional early-warning methods rely primarily on real-time parameter trends and historical baselines derived from the target well. Without offset-well knowledge providing prior guidance on the expected normal response envelope, these methods have difficulty distinguishing stuck-pipe precursors from normal response deviations caused by formation changes and progressive bit wear, which can lead to false alarms. Meanwhile, subtle and persistent early deviations may remain undetected. Consequently, alarms are often triggered only after risk signatures become pronounced, making the warning process essentially reactive. This limitation is particularly evident when limited target-well data are available. To address this limitation, this study proposes a formation- and bit-state-informed cross-well knowledge coupling framework for proactive stuck-pipe early warning. A sliding-window regression is first used to extract two parameters characterizing the local Torque–WOB relationship. Formation-dependent commonality, interwell variability, and spatial correlations of the dual features are modeled using a hierarchical Bayesian framework combined with Kriging, thereby providing a normal cross-well prior for an unseen target well. Historical bit-run information is then used to correct the prior according to the current bit-usage state. The corrected cross-well prior is dynamically coupled with target-well historical knowledge through precision weighting. Finally, the joint deviation of the real-time dual features from the expected normal state is quantified using the Mahalanobis distance, and an empirical threshold is used to trigger warnings. The framework was evaluated using leave-one-well-out validation on a database containing 81 wells from three drilling blocks and 29 documented stuck-pipe events. The coverage of normal target-well samples increased from 87.6% for the original cross-well prior to 90.2% after bit-state correction and further to 91.0% after knowledge coupling. Of the 13 events missed by the single-well model, 11 were recovered by the coupled model. The final model detected 27 of the 29 events, achieving a detection rate of 93.1%, a missed-event rate of 6.9%, and a false-alarm frequency of 2.1 alarms per 100 m. For successfully detected events, the mean warning lead distance was 4.6 m. Representative cases showed that warning activation could be traced to persistent migration of the α–β features and abnormal Torque growth under relatively stable WOB conditions. Sensitivity analysis further showed that the selected 20 m sliding window and baseline empirical threshold provided a reasonable balance among detection performance, false-alarm control, and warning lead distance. These results demonstrate that cross-well knowledge provides a stable and updateable external reference for target wells with limited historical data and supports interpretable, proactive stuck-pipe early warning.

nodes.name: Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: With the rapid development of aerospace technology, remote sensing images contain increasingly rich feature information, while large variations in object scales and imbalanced category distributions pose great challenges to remote sensing semantic segmentation. Current mainstream methods often rely on attention mechanisms for global modeling, yet they tend to over-average features, making it difficult to capture minority categories and preserve fine-grained details. To address these limitations, we propose a Dual Category-Guided Spatial Mamba Network (DGSMNet) that combines dual category guidance with a spatial Mamba mechanism. Specifically, a Dual-Stage Category Guidance (DSCG) module is designed to extract class information via wavelet transforms and guide feature learning, ensuring proportional representation of all categories across channels and enabling the model to learn underrepresented classes. In addition, a Spatial Mamba (SPM) module is introduced to enhance long-range modeling while retaining sensitivity to local details. By integrating DSCG and SPM, the proposed DGSMNet improves category-aware representation and spatial modeling on the evaluated benchmarks. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets demonstrate that DGSMNet achieves competitive performance among the compared methods.

nodes.name: Development of a Visual Digital Twin Dashboard for Two-Phase and Three-Phase Flow Regime Classification in Industrial Systems
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate classification of multiphase flow regimes is critical for efficient operation in energy and process industries. While significant progress has been made in two-phase flow classification, extending these techniques to three-phase systems introduces additional complexity due to interactions among phases and variations in flow geometry. In this study, we develop a visual digital-twin-based dashboard for real-time classification and visualization of flow regimes in both two-phase and three-phase flows. Experimental data were generated using the multiphase-flow facility at Hamad Bin Khalifa University, whose principal horizontal test section is approximately 6 m long with a 50.8-mm (2-in.) internal diameter and transparent acrylic sections for video observation. The two-phase water-air dataset contains 65 no-leak experiments spanning liquid superficial velocity from 1.0711 to 3.2134 m/s and gas superficial velocity from 0.6252 to 3.4041 m/s. The three-phase oil-water-air dataset contains 36 experiments spanning water superficial velocity from 1.4059 to 3.1427 m/s and air superficial velocity from 0.063 to 0.320 m/s, including 12 no-leak, 12 single-leak, and 12 dual-leak experiments. Flow dynamics were characterized using high-response dynamic pressure sensors to capture time-series pressure signals representative of multiphase flow behavior. In addition, high-speed imaging (up to 2000 frames per second) was employed to capture the visual characteristics of the flow regimes. Supporting measurements included thermocouples, differential pressure sensors, and electrical process tomography to enhance flow characterization. Visual inspection of the three-phase records reveals bubbly and dispersed structures that are more heterogeneous than those in the two-phase water-air reference data, motivating an analysis workflow that preserves the relationship among sensor signals, video, and operating conditions. These synchronized experimental records are organized as digital threads and streamed to the cloud-hosted digital twin software-as-a-service (SaaS) system. As pressure data arrive, deployed leak-detection models analyze the signals, and the visual twin dashboard presents the associated time series, pipeline video, operating state, and mapped detection or localization outputs for operator review. The MGSB two-phase model achieved a mean held-out detection F1 score of 0.930 +/- 0.082 and an F1 score of 0.783 +/- 0.110 under the prescribed input-corruption test. The MGSB three-phase model achieved an F1 score of 0.984, ROC AUC of 0.9987, false-alarm rate of 0.09%, and mean detection delay of 0.03 +/- 0.01 s on an eleven-experiment dual-orifice evaluation matrix. The novelty of this work lies in integrating experimental multiphase flow measurements with AI-based classification and a visual digital twin interface capable of identifying both two-phase and three-phase flow regimes across multiple geometries in real time. This framework provides a practical decision-support tool for industry applications, including pipeline monitoring, flow assurance, separator performance evaluation, and multiphase transport optimization in oil, gas, and broader process industries. By enabling rapid and reliable flow regime identification using minimal sensor inputs, the proposed system has the potential to significantly improve operational efficiency, reduce uncertainty in multiphase transport, and support next-generation digital oilfield applications.

nodes.name: Deep Guided Filtering and Detail Recovery-Based Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: To address the issues of poor detail clarity and limited visibility in infrared and visible image fusion under nighttime scenarios, this paper proposes a fusion method based on deep guided filtering and detail recovery. To fully exploit the multiscale features of source images, a multilevel image decomposition model is developed using deep guided filtering and Gaussian filtering, which further decomposes the high-frequency and low-frequency layers obtained by conventional multiscale decomposition into texture, saliency, and base information. In nighttime scenarios, these decomposed components typically suffer from blurring, low contrast, and insufficient brightness, making conventional fusion strategies inadequate for achieving satisfactory results. To cope with these challenges, three fusion strategies specifically tailored for nighttime imaging are devised: a texture information fusion strategy based on an enhancement function, a saliency information fusion strategy leveraging multi-contrast weights, and a base information fusion strategy that integrates the intensity transformation function of infrared images with grayscale difference analysis. To validate the performance of the proposed method, subjective and objective comparative evaluations are conducted on typical datasets including TNO, RoadScene, LLVIP, and MSRS, against classical fusion methods, state-of-the-art approaches, and methods specifically designed for nighttime imaging. Subjectively, the fused images produced by the proposed method exhibit richer and clearer details, along with more prominent thermal targets. Objectively, the proposed method demonstrates consistent advantages across eight metrics: average pixel intensity, standard deviation, average gradient, entropy, spatial frequency, total loss of information measure, perceptual saliency-based metric, and visual information fidelity. Both subjective and objective experimental results confirm that the proposed method can effectively accomplish nighttime image fusion tasks.

nodes.name: Contextual and structural representation learning for fine-grained barefoot footprint region recognition
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
nodes.abstract: Barefoot footprints provide valuable biometric evidence for forensic investigation and suspect identification. However, the rich structural details and diverse scale distributions of footprint images pose significant challenges for accurate fine-grained region recognition. Existing methods often struggle to effectively model contextual information and structural characteristics, limiting their ability to characterize subtle morphological variations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a robust framework for contextual–structural representation learning in barefoot footprint region recognition. A context-guided spatial feature reconstruction pyramid network (CGSFRPN) is introduced to enhance semantic consistency and feature interactions across different scales. To improve directional perception and edge detail modeling, a Direction-Aware Pinwheel Convolution (DAPConv) is incorporated to capture structural patterns with diverse orientations. Furthermore, a ConvFormer module based on the MetaFormer architecture is employed to facilitate efficient semantic representation and cross-region information integration. By jointly exploiting contextual information and structural characteristics, the proposed framework achieves robust recognition of fine-grained footprint regions, including toes, arches, and heels. Experiments conducted on a proprietary barefoot footprint dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 83.2%, outperforming several mainstream object detection approaches and exhibiting superior visualization performance. These results highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework for fine-grained barefoot footprint analysis and its potential applications in intelligent forensic identification.

nodes.name: ConLoRA-Sat: Parameter-Efficient Synthetic Satellite Imagery Generation for Data-Scarce Humanitarian Contexts
nodes.abstract: Data scarcity constrains Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) in regions such as the Horn of Africa. One example is United Nations peacekeeping training, which needs fictitious yet geographically plausible terrain rather than identifiable real locations. This article presents ConLoRA-Sat, a framework that generates satellite imagery with controllable land cover, together with a segmentation map for every generated image. The framework pairs Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with ControlNet on a Stable Diffusion XL backbone, adapting a general-purpose generative model to 0.5 m imagery from Mogadishu and Addis Ababa using only 322 training images. A segmentation model trained exclusively on synthetic imagery retains 90.1% of the real-data baseline, and supplementing 200 real images with 600 synthetic ones recovers 92.5% of full-data performance. In a perceptual study with 53 satellite imagery experts, synthetic images were misclassified as real in 20.8% of trials, and all three peacekeeping practitioners consulted stated that they would use the imagery to design training scenarios. The framework is released alongside an open pipeline and a curated dataset of more than 4,300 Horn of Africa image chips with paired segmentation maps and structured captions, offering a pathway for GeoAI in under-represented regions.

nodes.name: Closing the Loop: From Seismic to Dynamic and Back to Seismic, Iterations to Reach Spatial History Match
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract The objective of this project is closing the loop between seismic and dynamic modelling by creating static model based on seismic interpretations, bringing seismic data into the dynamic simulation, history matching spatial properties, then creating synthetic seismic to update the seismic model, and finally iterating in this loop to reach match between spatial properties. The goal is enhancing the reliability of predictions and estimate the next best time for a seismic survey. Pre-stack time-lapse (4D) seismic surveys were acquired for the study. Data QC and conditioning were performed; Bayesian inversion was then used to produce probability volumes for each vintage. The probability results were transferred in VDS format to the interactive deep learning seismic interpretation tool for plume identification. Geobodies were exported in RESCUE format, then imported into a numerical simulator for static and dynamic model building. Automated dynamic-seismic property history matching was performed to minimize quantitative error measured between spatial properties. Dynamic simulation generated output in RESCUE format and converted to elastic properties using petroelastic models to generate synthetic seismic. The established workflow was successfully applied on Sleipner CO2 dataset. Seismic plumes from 1999 to 2010 were used for history matching and as a validation for reservoir simulation. Results of dynamic model were used to create simulated seismic and matched with real observed seismic. During this iterative process, dynamic, petroelastic, and time to depth conversion models were updated. Finally, dynamic forecast modelling could be used to generate forward seismic to define the best time for a new monitor survey. Linking spatial properties to seismic is a challenge. Cross disciplinary integration is required to match 4D seismic and dynamic modelling. While 1D workflows from seismic to dynamic and vice versa have been tested in literature, a closed loop workflow and the iteration to achieve spatial history matching in both seismic images and dynamic simulation is novel. Once correlation between seismic and reservoir performance is established, it could be used as a reasonable justification for further monitoring surveys.

nodes.name: CSP-Mamba: prototype-involved spatial-spectral Mamba for hyperspectral image classification
nodes.venue: Journal of Electronic Imaging
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral image classification requires effective spatial-spectral modeling and reliable pixel-wise predictions. This paper proposes CSP-Mamba, a framework that combines input calibration, spatial-spectral encoding, and prototype-guided classification. Before sequence encoding, embedded features are calibrated using adjacent-band spectral priors and multiscale spatial context with residual-controlled adaptive fusion. The encoder combines row-wise spatial modeling and grouped spectral modeling with adjacent-band compensation and integrates the two branches through base-offset fusion. A dual-head classifier then uses class prototypes to guide feature refinement and combines prototype-based and convolution-based predictions. Experiments on four public hyperspectral datasets demonstrate competitive classification performance. Additional paired and region-wise analyses examine the statistical reliability and spatial behavior of the predictions.

nodes.name: An explainable graph transformer framework integrating structural reasoning and visual attention for interpretable nail disease diagnosis
nodes.venue: Discover Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract Automated nail-disease classification remains a challenging task as different nail disorders present subtle and overlapping variations in color, texture and morphology. This paper introduces GraphX, an explainable graph-transformer framework that improves the baseline Graph Vision Transformer by incorporating image-specific graph construction, graph-transformer fusion, and attention guidance during training. The Adaptive Graph Construction module constructs a sparse graph per image based on the cosine similarity of spatially and texture enriched patch representations and retains the eight most similar neighbors per patch. The Cross-Attention Fusion module allows reciprocal refinement between graph-based structural embeddings and transformer-based contextual tokens. The Explainability-Aware Attention module learns to match the attention distribution with continuous lesion-prior maps generated from local intensity contrast and color deviation, providing weak spatial guidance without dermatologist-annotated lesion mask. In classification, GraphX achieved 94.97% accuracy and macro-averaged one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.98, which outperformed the baseline models evaluated. Explainability was measured with Grad-CAM visualization, normalized attribution entropy, and deletion–insertion faithfulness testing. The results demonstrate strong internal classification performance and provide preliminary evidence of model’s attention patterns, highlighting the potential of GraphX as a transparent framework for automated nail disease classification.

nodes.name: An End-To-End Multimodal VLM Framework for Automated PPE Annotation and Site-Aware SOP Compliance Monitoring
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Traditional computer vision systems for Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) monitoring are constrained by labour-intensive manual labelling and limited contextual awareness. Conventional models identify isolated objects but lack an understanding of spatial layout, equipment states, and procedural logic. As a result, organizations that rely on these systems often find themselves managing a narrow slice of their actual safety exposure: a helmet is either present or absent, a glove is either detected or not, but the surrounding context, whether that equipment is being used correctly, in the right sequence, under the right conditions, remains invisible to the model. This paper presents a centrally hosted, end-to-end AI framework that automates the lifecycle of safety monitoring using a Multimodal Vision-Language Model (VLM). The framework utilizes a foundation VLM to autonomously generate structured training datasets, eliminating manual annotation bottlenecks that have historically slowed the deployment of computer-vision-based safety tools. These datasets facilitate both the training of lightweight convolutional networks and the site-specific fine-tuning of targeted VLMs, allowing organizations to choose the deployment profile that best matches their hardware and latency constraints. By embedding contextual intelligence and procedural reasoning derived from Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into the model's visual grounding, the framework establishes an adaptive paradigm for AI-driven safety monitoring, shifting the industry closer to its "Goal Zero" safety ambitions, the aspiration that no incident, however minor, should be considered an acceptable cost of operations.

nodes.name: A privacy-aware multimodal framework for assessing difficult aerobics actions using dual-attention CNN and blockchain governance
nodes.venue: Asia Conference on Edge Intelligence and Service Computing (EISC 2026)
nodes.abstract: Accurate assessment of high-difficulty aerobics actions requires reliable motion recognition together with secure management of sensitive training data, yet existing systems seldom achieve both within a unified framework. This paper presents a privacy-aware multimodal architecture integrating a Dual-Attention Multi-Channel Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network (DA-MCMS-CNN) with a permissioned blockchain for training-record governance. The network jointly leverages RGB video and wireless Channel State Information (CSI) to capture subtle spatio-temporal patterns in difficult aerobics skills, while dual-attention mechanisms enhance feature learning across channels and spatial locations, and the blockchain layer orchestrates identity verification, role-based access control and tamper-evident logging through smart contracts. Evaluation on public human-action benchmarks and a self-constructed aerobics dataset shows improved recognition accuracy, stable tracking, and real-time operation with low access latency.

A Smartphone-Assisted Schirmer Strip for Rapid Dual Colorimetric Sensing of Tear Glucose and pH Level
nodes.venue: ACS Omega
nodes.abstract: Abstract Although tear biomarkers are routinely determined using various clinical methods, most current techniques are complex, time-consuming, and require expensive equipment. Therefore, point-of-care (POC) testing is attracting considerable attention for rapid and noninvasive analyses. Here, we present a dual-function colorimetric Schirmer strip for the simultaneous determination of tear glucose and pH using the naked eye and image processing software. In our approach, horseradish peroxidase-glucose oxidase nanoflowers (HRP–GOx@NF) are used for glucose detection, and red cabbage-derived anthocyanins are used as a pH-sensitive, nontoxic indicator. In glucose detection, the catalytic stepwise reaction of HRP–GOx@NF produced a distinct blue color within 30 s by enabling the rapid oxidation of 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) in the presence of glucose, and this optimized platform exhibited a visual detection limit of 0.5 mM. Additionally, the anthocyanin-modified Schirmer strip simultaneously displayed distinct color transitions in response to varying pH values of the artificial tear fluid. This work presents a novel multiparametric paper platform that uniquely upgrades standard Schirmer strips for simultaneous, single-step tear collection, glucose sensing, and pH mapping without altering fluid flow. Like this, it demonstrates a rapid, cost-effective, and easy-to-prepare diagnostic tool offering significant advantages over conventional methods.

nodes.name: A High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Building Extraction Model Based on Spectral Index Gated Attention and Transfer Learning
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing building extraction often requires large amounts of manually labeled data, and models trained on one dataset may not perform equally well on another without additional annotations. To reduce this dependency on labeled target data, we propose SIGA-UNet3+, which combines a Spectral Index Gated Attention (SIGA) module with a transfer learning strategy. The SIGA module fuses DSBI, NDVI, and NDWI to emphasize building features and suppress vegetation/water interference. Pre-training on the public SpaceNet dataset followed by fine-tuning on a self-built GF-2 dataset (Changchun, China) allows the model to adapt with limited local labels. On SpaceNet, SIGA-UNet3+ achieves F1 = 83.21% and IoU = 70.19%, obtaining the best overall segmentation performance among the compared methods. On the GF-2 dataset, it attains F1 = 84.56% and IoU = 72.17%. Moreover, using only 10% of the GF-2 training samples, transfer learning improves the F1 score by 6–8 percentage points compared to training from scratch. These results indicate that SIGA-UNet3+ can provide a promising and data-efficient approach for high-resolution remote sensing building extraction.

nodes.name: A Conditional Variational Autoencoder Surrogate for High-Fidelity Spatiotemporal Prediction of Hydraulic Fracturing Dynamics and Proppant Distribution
nodes.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Comprehensive evaluation of hydraulic fracturing demands spatially resolved mapping of proppant transport, the evolution of effective conductivity across the pay zone, and inter-cluster competition driven by stress shadowing. While high-fidelity, fully coupled three-dimensional simulators yield this requisite spatial resolution, their steep computational expense for multi-stage well evaluations makes iterative design screening and optimization workflows intractable. For example, a single five-cluster stage requires approximately five minutes of compute time, accumulating to roughly two hours for a standard 24-stage well. To overcome this limitation, this study introduces a conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE) trained on high-fidelity fracture simulations to predict two-dimensional proppant concentration and effective conductivity maps produced by the hydraulic stimulation across all clusters in under one second per stage. From these high-resolution, end-of-pumping spatial fields, key operational metrics can be deterministically extracted, including proppant cutoff length, flowing fracture length, and fracture height. To generate the training dataset, a Python automation framework was developed to interface with a fully coupled, high-fidelity numerical simulator. This framework executed thousands of realizations capturing the geologic and operational parameter space of the DJ Basin. Operational inputs, namely injection rate and pumped volume, were generated using Latin Hypercube Sampling, while geological properties were assigned using a zone-aware layered distribution to preserve localized stratigraphy and mechanical contrasts. Ultimately, the trained surrogate generates ten two-dimensional maps per stage realization, comprising five proppant concentration and five effective conductivity fields. This single-stage architecture is inherently modular, providing a foundational unit for full-well, multistage evaluations. The surrogate model achieves a computational speedup of more than two orders of magnitude, reducing the evaluation time for a full 24-stage well from approximately two hours to less than 30 seconds. When evaluated on unseen validation datasets, the surrogate achieves an end-of-pumping Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.03 lb/ft2 for proppant concentration and 0.01 md-ft for effective conductivity. Furthermore, the generated spatial fields accurately capture complex geomechanical behaviors, including cluster-level stress shadowing and mechanically confined height growth. By training on fully coupled simulator outputs enforcing stress shadowing, mechanical-layer height confinement, and mass-balance-governed proppant transport, the surrogate preserves governing physics without explicit physics-informed loss terms. The automated simulation-to-training pipeline removes the manual bottleneck of dataset generation from commercial simulators and is extensible to other unconventional shale plays requiring hydraulic stimulation. The modular single-stage architecture enables direct extension to multistage wells, reducing full-well evaluation from hours to seconds, though multistage deployment will need to account for the evolving stress state from sequential pumping, where prior-stage fractures alter local stresses and can reshape subsequent fracture geometry.

nodes.name: Reproduction of substorm auroral currents in the ionosphere using a machine-learning-based emulator and SuperDARN data assimilation
nodes.venue: Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate
nodes.abstract: Auroral electrojet dynamics during isolated substorms are reproduced using a machine-learning-based emulator with SuperDARN data assimilation. Representing such short-timescale variability is important for improving space-weather prediction relevant to technological systems. Reproducing this variability remains challenging for the SMRAI emulator (Surrogate Model for the REPPU Auroral Ionosphere; Kataoka et al., 2024, https://doi.org/10.1029/2023SW003720), where REPPU is the REProduce Plasma Universe global magnetohydrodynamic simulation. SMRAI is trained on ionospheric outputs from a REPPU MHD simulation and primarily produces smooth and gradual variations in auroral currents during substorms. Therefore, we evaluate the performance of SMRAI with SuperDARN line-of-sight velocity data assimilation (Nakano et al.,2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025SW004488), referred to as the SMRAI–SD framework. Two isolated substorm events on 30 and 31 October 2023 are analyzed to assess the performance of the SMRAI–SD. The SMRAI–SD reproduces auroral current variability in closer agreement with observations than SMRAI, as indicated by improved correspondence with the AL and AU indices. Although reproducing AE indices is not the primary objective, they are used to evaluate the performance of the SMRAI–SD approach and to identify its strengths and limitations through comparison with observations and examination of two-dimensional maps of ionospheric electric potential. SMRAI–SD reproduces abrupt changes in the ionospheric potential that are more pronounced than in the SMRAI. This study therefore evaluates whether such abrupt electrodynamic changes are physically consistent and under what conditions they are reliable. The results demonstrate that SuperDARN data assimilation enhances the ability of the SMRAI model to reproduce ionospheric auroral electrodynamics during substorm and supports its application to space-weather forecasting studies.

Multimodal expressions of mathematical thinking in play-based contexts: Recognising young children’s mathematical competence beyond numbers
nodes.venue: Set: Research Information for Teachers
nodes.abstract: Early mathematical thinking is often missed when assessment focuses only on numbers and symbols. This article explores how young children express mathematical ideas through multiple modes in play-based contexts, including gesture, drawing, construction, movement, and interaction with materials. Drawing on social semiotics, embodied learning, and play-based pedagogy, this article highlights how children engage in mathematical thinking and communication through pattern, spatial reasoning, symmetry, and problem solving. The analysis emphasises the importance of teacher noticing and intentional responses in recognising and extending these moments. It also foregrounds culturally and linguistically diverse ways of knowing, arguing for a broader, more inclusive understanding of early mathematical competence grounded in everyday activity.

nodes.name: FEATS-G: Orbit and quantum sensor performance simulation for future satellite gravity missions
nodes.venue: GRACE/GRACE-FO Science Team Meeting 2026
nodes.abstract: Satellite gravimetry missions GRACE and GRACE-FO have significantly advanced Earth observation by enabling monthly, high-precision mapping of global mass redistributions. These missions have provided unprecedented insights into the system Earth, such as ice sheet and glacier mass loss, sea level rise, terrestrial water storage changes. However, the classical electrostatic accelerometers suffer from their low-frequency drift and are one of the limiting factors. This drawback can be counterbalanced by an accelerometer based on Cold Atom Interferometry (CAI) because of its high long-term stability.The FEATS-G project advances this frontier through end-to-end simulations to evaluate quantum-based satellite mission concepts. The simulations allow for a comprehensive evaluation of future mission concepts and the exploration of novel scientific applications. They also enable the assessment of quantum-based sensors’ added value in distinguishing between different geophysical signals, while preparing the scientific community for the arrival of this new data type.This contribution focuses on the simulation procedure of observations based on quantum technology. The selected mission scenario will be simulated by the orbit propagation software VENQS. The satellites’ surface is modelled by means of finite elements in order to calculate precise non-gravitational forces induced by solar and Earth radiation and atmospheric drag. The non-gravitational accelerations are considered as disturbance and are measured by the accelerometer. The CAI acceleration measurements are simulated considering various error sources, such as detection noise, contrast loss, wavefront aberration and laser frequency noise. Furthermore, rotational effects and rotation compensation methods using a counter-rotating mirror are included. The simulation procedure and methodology and first results are shown. The artificial orbit data and sensor output will later be used in the gravity field recovery process.We acknowledge the support by the European Union for the project FEATS-G (Call: HORIZON-CL4-2025-02-SPACE-81).

nodes.name: An integrated deep learning approach for 3D urban scene generation using monocular satellite imagery
nodes.venue: Journal of Computer & Electrical and Electronics Engineering Sciences
nodes.abstract: Aims: The aim of this study is to build a pipeline leveraging deep learning for 3D reconstruction of urban environments using only single high-resolution satellite images, while comparing strengths and weaknesses of the proposed system with its alternatives like multi-view or LiDAR-based methods. Methods: We proposed a pipeline system consisting of several steps with different deep learning models. Each step works independently to complete different tasks. Firstly, the system generates Digital Surface Model (DSM) using a Pix2Pix conditional GAN with perceptual loss, then a Mask R-CNN model is used to build segmentation and finally a ResNet-50 model classifies roof type of buildings. Models were trained on SpaceNet Urban 3D, Inria Aerial Labeling, and GATE roof datasets, and MSE, IoU/mAP and Accuracy/F1 scores are preferred as evaluation metrics for elevation accuracy, segmentation quality and classification performance, respectively. Results: DSM generation achieved MSE of 986.70 (mean absolute deviation of 31 gray levels), with 90% of pixels maintaining errors below 50 levels. Instance segmentation attained 0.712 mAP@IoU50, declining to 0.358 at stricter IoU75 thresholds, revealing boundary precision challenges. Roof classification reached 80% accuracy with strong performance on common types (hip roofs: F1=0.91). The system synthesizes these outputs into exportable 3D scenes combining terrain meshes, extruded building geometries, and vegetation elements. Conclusion: This work validates that monocular satellite imagery can be sufficiently used as a sole input for a system using different deep learning models to generate functionally useful 3D urban models. The proposed system offers a practical solution for rapid urban analysis when additional data like multi-view image or laser scan is unavailable. The coordinated integration of multiple deep learning components yields promising results for urban reconstruction using conventional satellite imagery while geometric precision remains below production-grade standards.

AI-Driven Object Detection for Projectile Localization on Trauma X-rays: An Analytical Study of Diagnostic Accuracy and Forensic Utility
nodes.venue: Indian Journal of Forensic Medicine & Toxicology
nodes.abstract: Background: Trauma radiographs may reveal retained bullets or metallic fragments, and early localization can influence further imaging, surgical planning, safety assessment, and forensic documentation. Methods: This feasibility study used a fully synthetic, computer-generated tabular dataset of 400 case-level records divided into 240 training-design records, 60 validation-design records, and a 100-record held-out test set. The 400 records were not pixel-level radiographs: no DICOM, PNG, or other X-ray images were generated for model training, and no YOLOv9 neural network was trained. Instead, ground-truth labels, confidence scores, simulated detector outputs, a simulated time-constrained radiologist first pass, object-level matches, and processing times were produced by a fixed-seed probabilistic simulation (seed 9173) to demonstrate an evaluation framework. The test set comprised 70 projectile-positive and 30 projectile-negative records. Results: The simulated AI output yielded 65 true positives, 5 false negatives, 3 false positives, and 27 true negatives, corresponding to 92.0% accuracy, 92.9% sensitivity, 90.0% specificity, 95.6% precision, and a 94.2% F1 score; ROC-AUC was 0.972. The simulated radiologist first pass was correct in 83.0% of test records. In paired correctness analysis, AI alone was correct in 12 records and the radiologist alone in 3 (exact McNemar p=0.035). Of 145 synthetic annotated fragments, 136 were matched, with mean IoU 0.828, mAP@0.50=0.937, and mAP@0.50:0.95=0.593. Conclusion: These values are simulation outputs and do not constitute evidence that YOLOv9 detects projectiles on patient radiographs. The study demonstrates a reproducible analysis plan that requires validation on authentic multicentre radiographs, independent annotation, external testing, calibration, human-factors evaluation, and forensic governance before any clinical use.
